key_insight: GradAudit uses parameter gradients to audit vision-language models, separating training pairs from non-training data by detecting stable, aligned gradient signatures.
clinical_relevance: In healthcare, this could help identify whether sensitive patient image-report pairs were used in model training, supporting privacy and provenance checks.
method: Examines internal gradient behavior instead of only model outputs.
Compares gradient stability and alignment for suspected training samples vs non-training samples.
Looks for genuine image-text association learning in VLLMs.
evidence_signal: Across medical and general-domain datasets, the method outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in both pretraining and fine-tuning settings, and revealed more unauthorized data use than prior methods in a copyrighted-content case study.
watch_item: Gradient-based auditing may be computationally heavier and still requires careful interpretation, especially when applied to real healthcare systems with diverse data distributions.
paper_title: Revealing Training Data Exposure in Vision Language Large Models via Parameter Gradients
